# PackageSetupWindow

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Setup` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Setup/PackageSetupWindow.cs#L33)

The face of "Set Up Project for VR": which steps the next run takes, what the run is doing
now, and what each step ended up reporting.

The setup used to be two menu items and a console to squint at - one to start it, a second
one that only lit up while it was running so it could be cancelled, and no way to see how
far along it was. All of that is here now, which is why the cancel menu item is gone: a
button that is only ever needed while a run is in progress belongs next to the run.

Between runs the steps are listed in two groups, by [`SetupScope`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupScope), each with
a box to tick. Somebody who has just cloned a project that was set up elsewhere has its
project half already and needs only this machine's, and a project that was set up long
ago may want one step again rather than all of them. During a run the list is the run
itself, in the order it goes.

The window owns nothing but the ticks. The sequence lives in [`PackageSetup`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/PackageSetup)
and its state in [`Progress`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupRunner#progress), which is kept in SessionState
precisely so that closing this window, or the script reloads the setup causes, cannot lose
track of a running setup.
